events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The cancellation was made by the rider [F2], so NS-0 routes the case to the instant-booking rider-cancellation branch NS-4. The timeline shows acceptance at 14:05:00 and rider cancellation at 14:07:55, i.e. 175 seconds later [F2]. NS-4 provides that all cancellations made within 3 minutes of matching are not chargeable, so the $6.61 fee on record [F5] fails at the threshold [NS-0][NS-4]. This is the trace's settled ✗ element — the "no charge" condition is met — and it alone resolves the dispute.

No other ground can sustain the fee. NS-1 requires, cumulatively, that the driver pressed "I'm Here" (i), that GPS placed him within the pickup zone (ii), and that he waited over 3 minutes there (iii) [NS-1]. The driver never tapped "I'm Here" [F4], never entered the 200 m pickup radius (closest approach 1685 m) [F1], and the platform never recorded an arrival [F3]; so (i)(ii)(iii) all fail and the NS-2 refund follows [NS-2]. Consistently, the driver's own statement says only that he was on his way [F9] — no no-show is alleged, and NS-0 lists no other ground for the fee [NS-0].

The driver's chat "About 5 min, traffic" [F8] and the speed-band reading on Nassim Road (band 3, 20–29 km/h) [F10], with no incidents recorded [F11] and fair weather [F12], do not excuse the failure to arrive and do not supply the missing NS-1 elements [NS-1][NS-4]. System records (GPS closest approach, null arrival, null "I'm Here" tap) [F1][F3][F4] control over the chat and the driver statement [F8][F9].

Amount: the cancellation fee of record is $6.61 with no surge (1.0×) [F5][F6]; per NS-7 the refund is issued as a voucher of that value [NS-7]. NS-2's fraud add-on is not triggered because no "I'm Here" tap was ever recorded [F4], so no account flag is warranted [NS-2]. Profile facts [F13][F14] do not decide the case and are not used to flag either party.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: You were charged a $6.61 cancellation fee. We've reversed it. The charge doesn't apply because you cancelled about three minutes after matching — within the window where a cancellation isn't chargeable — and the driver never arrived at your pickup point or marked himself as arrived. So the fee comes off your record. The $6.61 is being credited to you as a Ryde voucher of that amount; you don't need to do anything, and there's no action against your account. Nothing else changes for you.

DRIVER: The $6.61 cancellation fee charged to the rider has been refunded, issued as a Ryde voucher. The charge didn't apply because the rider cancelled roughly three minutes after matching, within the no-charge window, and the records show you weren't marked as arrived at the pickup point. No action is being taken against your account — nothing is flagged and your standing is unaffected. You can keep taking trips as usual.

ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation was made by the rider [F2], so NS-0 routes the case to the instant-booking rider-cancellation branch NS-4. The timeline shows acceptance at 14:05:00 and rider cancellation at 14:07:55, i.e. 175 seconds later [F2]. NS-4 provides that all cancellations made within 3 minutes of matching are not chargeable, so the $6.61 fee on record [F5] fails at the threshold [NS-0][NS-4]. This is the trace's settled ✗ element — the "no charge" condition is met — and it alone resolves the dispute.

No other ground can sustain the fee. NS-1 requires, cumulatively, that the driver pressed "I'm Here" (i), that GPS placed him within the pickup zone (ii), and that he waited over 3 minutes there (iii) [NS-1]. The driver never tapped "I'm Here" [F4], never entered the 200 m pickup radius (closest approach 1685 m) [F1], and the platform never recorded an arrival [F3]; so (i)(ii)(iii) all fail and the NS-2 refund follows [NS-2]. Consistently, the driver's own statement says only that he was on his way [F9] — no no-show is alleged, and NS-0 lists no other ground for the fee [NS-0].

The driver's chat "About 5 min, traffic" [F8] and the speed-band reading on Nassim Road (band 3, 20–29 km/h) [F10], with no incidents recorded [F11] and fair weather [F12], do not excuse the failure to arrive and do not supply the missing NS-1 elements [NS-1][NS-4]. System records (GPS closest approach, null arrival, null "I'm Here" tap) [F1][F3][F4] control over the chat and the driver statement [F8][F9].

Amount: the cancellation fee of record is $6.61 with no surge (1.0×) [F5][F6]; per NS-7 the refund is issued as a voucher of that value [NS-7]. NS-2's fraud add-on is not triggered because no "I'm Here" tap was ever recorded [F4], so no account flag is warranted [NS-2]. Profile facts [F13][F14] do not decide the case and are not used to flag either party.

The rider's no-show dispute history [F13] and the driver's trip volume/rating [F14] are profile facts, which under the procedural rules cannot decide the case; the outcome turns on the driver's GPS and button records [F1][F3][F4] under NS-1/NS-2/NS-4.

The driver's point that band 3 traffic [F10] is outside the severe range and that no incident was recorded [F11] is not adverse to the rider's outcome: it confirms no reasonable-cause excuse exists under NS-1, so the fee still fails [NS-1][NS-4].

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s after acceptance, i.e. within the 3-minute window in which Ryde charges no cancellation fee, so the $6.61 fee should never have been levied.
The driver was 1685 m away and never entered the 200 m pickup radius at any point, so no no-show, arrival or waiting basis for a fee exists.
The driver never tapped "I'm Here", which is a mandatory precondition for any waiting-time or no-show charge against the rider.

The driver has never claimed the rider was a no-show — his statement only says he was on his way when the rider cancelled — so the fee falls outside the only two grounds on which a cancellation fee may be charged.

The rider's own contemporaneous conduct corroborates that the driver had not arrived: at 14:05 she asked for the ETA and the driver answered "About 5 min, traffic", which is still outstanding when she cancelled 2 min 55 s later.
No traffic incident or severe congestion is recorded on the route during the trip window, so the driver's "traffic" explanation cannot convert his failure to arrive into a chargeable cancellation.
The fee was charged with no surge multiplier applied (1.0x), so the $6.61 is the standard cancellation fee and the full $6.61 is the amount in dispute, refundable as a voucher under NS-7.

The driver's GPS record shows he never reached the pickup point while he had pressed no arrival button; the incident should also be sent to Ryde account review in view of his other unupheld no-show dispute record.

weaknesses: The 2 min 55 s cancellation is only 5 seconds inside the free-cancellation cut-off, so the other side will argue the timing is borderline and that the rider pre-empted a driver who was, per his chat message (F8), about 5 minutes away — which does not by itself justify a fee but invites sympathy for the driver.

The rider's profile shows 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days (F13); the driver will use this to portray the rider as a repeat canceller, though NS-2 turns on the driver's GPS and button records (F1, F4), not the rider's history.

The driver's statement (F9) does not concede fault and could be read as him still being en route; the rider has no record of the driver refusing the trip, so the driver may argue the cancellation was purely the rider's choice — an argument that nevertheless fails because he was 1685 m away (F1) and never pressed "I'm Here" (F4).

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 55 s (175 s) after acceptance, i.e. within the 3-minute window, so under the instant-booking rider-cancellation branch the fee is not chargeable.
The $6.61 cancellation fee is on record and was collected (no surge applied), so the amount at stake is exactly $6.61.

The driver never entered the pickup zone (closest approach 1685 m, never within 200 m) and the platform never recorded an arrival, so my client cannot sustain a no-show claim under NS-1 (ii) and the fee cannot rest on rider no-show.

The driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so NS-1 (i) is also unmet; the cancellation is therefore governed by NS-3, under which the passenger bears no cancellation fee and the driver's cancellation is instead counted in the driver's cancellation rate as an account matter.

The driver's own chat message says he was "About 5 min" away at 14:06, which is consistent with the GPS record that he was still ~1.7 km out when the rider cancelled at 14:07:55 — the rider had a genuine, record-backed basis to cancel.

No traffic incident was recorded near the route and the only speed-band reading (Nassim Road band 3, 20-29 km/h) is outside the band 1-2 severe range, so stop-and-go traffic does not excuse the failure to reach the pickup point within 3 minutes even if the chat mentions "traffic".

The driver has 666 trips in 90 days, a 4.5 rating and 0 upheld disputes in 90 days, while the rider has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days; this supports a swift full refund rather than an account sanction against my client.

weaknesses: The chat (F8: "About 5 min, traffic") and the driver's statement (F9: "I was on my way when the rider cancelled") are the only driver-side explanations, but the GPS record (F1: closest approach 1685 m, never within 200 m) and the timeline (F3: driver_arrived_at null; F4: no "I'm Here" tap) override them - I cannot argue the driver was at the pickup point.

NS-3 records the driver's cancellation without a valid reason as an account matter and NS-3's cancellation-rate threshold (>17.5%) can suspend an account; F14 shows a high 90-day trip volume, so the other side may point to this cancellation as a driver conduct issue even though the fee refund is due to the rider.

The rider cancelled at 14:07:55, only 5 seconds before the 3-minute mark (F2), so if the clock were measured from any later event the NS-4 free-cancellation window would close and the fee would stand; NS-4's start point (matching) is the strongest reading but is the one fact I most depend on.

points.response: Agreed and relied upon: the 175-second cancellation in F2 falls inside the free-cancellation window of NS-4, which is precisely why the $6.61 must come back.
No dispute on quantum: F5 and F6 fix the disputed amount at exactly $6.61 with no surge, which is the voucher amount sought under NS-7.
Accepted as far as it goes: the 1685 m closest approach and the null arrival record in F1 and F3 defeat any no-show case under NS-1(ii), so the fee has no basis and NS-2 requires full refund.

I adopt F4 — the missing "I'm Here" tap means NS-1(i) fails and the cancellation falls to be refunded in full under NS-2 (NS-3 governs driver-initiated cancellations, not this rider cancellation), so no fee can be retained.

This point supports the rider: the driver's own 14:06 message of "About 5 min" (F8) read with the GPS fix of 1685 m at 14:07:55 (F1) shows he could not possibly have been at the pickup point by the time of cancellation (F2).
Agreed: F10's Nassim Road reading of 20-29 km/h is band 3, outside the band 1-2 severe range, and F11 records no incident, so "traffic" (F8) cannot manufacture a chargeable no-show.

I do not seek any account flag against the driver, so his 666 trips, 4.5 rating and 0 upheld disputes (F14) need not be weighed; I withdraw C8's flag request and ask only that the rider's $6.61 be refunded as a voucher per NS-7.
Rider withdraws claim C8 (the account-flag request against the driver), since NS-2's flag trigger requires a falsely pressed "I'm Here" button, which F4 shows did not occur here.

Conceded; I read the same clock (F2, 175 s after acceptance) and the same fare record (F5) and NS-0/NS-4 give the rider the free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 cannot stand. My client's interest is in the cleanest possible disposition, which for a driver with no arrival record (F3, F4) is a full refund without any conduct finding against him.

Conceded that no fee basis exists on the driver's side: the GPS shows a closest approach of 1685 m and never within 200 m (F1) and the platform recorded no arrival (F3), so NS-1 (ii) fails and NS-2's refund follows.

Conceded; driver_pressed_here_at is null (F4), so NS-1 (i) is unmet — but the same fact shows the driver pressed no false arrival button, so NS-2's fraud add-on (which needs a “I'm Here” tap recorded while off-pickup) is not triggered against him.

Accepted on the record: my client's statement says only that he was on his way (F9) and never alleges a no-show, so NS-0 leaves the fee without a ground and it should be refunded in full rather than litigated further.

Not contested, and it is consistent with the system records rather than adverse to my client: the driver's "About 5 min" at 14:06 (F8) matches the GPS position ~1.7 km away at 14:07:55 (F1, F2), so the message shows no misrepresentation of arrival.

Conceded; no incident was recorded and the only band reading is band 3 (F10, F11, F12), so my client has no traffic justification to offer and I withdraw any suggestion that the delay excuses a charge.

Conceded as to the amount and remedy: no surge applied (F6) and the fee of record is $6.61 (F5), so the full $6.61 is the sum to be returned as a voucher under NS-7 — my client does not oppose that outcome.

This is the one rider point I oppose: NS-2's account-flag add-on requires a recorded “I'm Here” tap while outside the pickup radius, and F4 shows no tap at all, so no abuse of the arrival/waiting button occurred; the rider cites F14 but that is the driver's own profile with 0 upheld disputes in 90 days, which cannot be used alone to decide this case.
